avoid: Treating screen or preliminary scores as sufficient evidence when seed-consistency validation fails, as in D.
Expanding S with additional families before measuring overlap and marginal yield within its two existing branches.
Returning to narrow single-geometry proposals such as A, C, or E without a demonstrated complementary lane.
Assuming that signature targeting alone will improve catalogue coverage without benchmark evidence, as B did not reach that stage.
Claiming discriminant progress from blank fields or from the inconsistent prior summary; the reported benchmarked candidates show zero improvements where values are present.
Inferring the identities of hidden seeds, groups, or group–signature pairs from aggregate counts.
generation_feedback.diagnosis: S won because it converted the strongest ideas from A and E into one coherent orbit-polynomial portfolio. It produced 5 fresh missing pairs, 166 fresh pair hits, and all 60 fresh seed hits—clearly exceeding A’s 2/98/58 and E’s 2/18/15. The complementary geometries mattered: the signed-cube branch supplied stronger discovery density, while the quadratic–quartic branch supplied broader group coverage and better verification. A showed that signed-cube geometry is productive but insufficient alone; E’s Cartesian composita added useful but weaker complementary reach. D’s portfolio-repair idea earned strong preliminary scores but failed seed consistency and ultimately delivered only 2 fresh pairs from 2 seeds, so its apparent promise did not translate into robust performance. B’s signature-chamber proposal and C’s GL(2,3) construction were pruned before benchmark evidence established broad value. No reported finalist produced a discriminant improvement, so the generation improved catalogue coverage rather than low-discriminant records. The previous feedback’s larger aggregate counts and claimed discriminant gains are inconsistent with the supplied generation results and should not guide the next iteration.
generation_feedback.next_generation_direction: Start from S and run a fixed-budget ablation/rebalancing experiment over its two branches. Partition each branch into explicit parameter sublanes, record only aggregate verification rate, fresh-pair hits, fresh missing-pair count, and discriminant improvements, then remove sublanes whose marginal discoveries are redundant. Reallocate most recovered budget to new forced-action geometries outside signed cubes and 4×2 Cartesian products, while reserving a small fixed quota for an independently verified discriminant-focused control. Require every proposed addition to beat the retained S sublanes on marginal missing-pair yield across repeated seed batches before it enters the portfolio.
what_worked: Combining two explicitly complementary permutation geometries in a shared orbit-polynomial framework.
Prioritizing signed-cube orbits for discovery: the reported branch comparison favored them with 3 new pairs and 102 fresh-pair hits.
Retaining quadratic–quartic Cartesian orbits for their higher verification rate and wider group coverage.
Preserving broad seed reach: S achieved fresh hits on all 60 seeds while improving missing-pair discovery.
Using forced-action structure to target proper transitive subgroups instead of relying on generic full-group behavior.
